content: Treat every elder as your own grandparent, every contemporary as your sibling, and every child as your own son or daughter.
author: Native American Proverbs
explanation: When society collapses into atomized, lonely individuals, everyone treats strangers with suspicion and cold indifference. The traditional clan system expanded the family circle to encompass the entire tribe: no child was an orphan, and no elder was abandoned in an empty room. Rebuild the circle.
practicalInsight: Look at an unfamiliar elder, stranger, or child today through the lens of family kinship. Offer protective warmth.
reflectionPrompt: How would your daily behavior change if you treated every stranger on the street as your direct family?
